Each primitive represents a distinct operational kernel: tackle probability models encode conditional likelihoods of defensive success, pass rush win rates quantify defensive effectiveness through tracking-derived zones, and rush over expected v2 compares empirical outcomes to predictive baselines. These operators are dualized into GSI’s Bayesian inference framework, where each metric becomes a probabilistic observation linked to latent tactical states. Their failure modes stem from tracking resolution limitations or misalignment between model assumptions and real-world dynamics. The epistemic trace reveals that these primitives are not merely descriptive but constitute methodological scaffolding for future integration of raw tracking data once access is granted.
